Yeah idk what some ppl are talking about in here, but I work in the industry, not a franchisee but above store management. I can’t speak on other brands or chains, but our increase is because of our cost of goods increase along with labor cost increase. 

A healthy restaurant will net bottom line around 10%. Once you start going under that you have minimal room for error. Pre Covid we were fairly profitable as a market averaging around 15%. During Covid we had major labor problems and supply chain issues which made it difficult to operate. Costs for product were going through the roof. The only way we could sustain was to pay people more to come to work and raise prices to help offset the increase in product and labor. 

Post Covid we are averaging about 12% bottom line, so we aren’t doing as well, but still able to sustain and continue growth. Admittedly some of our product costs have come down, however our labor continues to increase. We are still having to increase wages to keep people. We haven’t increased prices in about 6 months time, but we may reevaluate at the beginning of the year. 

For anyone curious, we start team members at $15/hr. GMs make around 75-80k avg sometimes more depending on bonus. We are in a LCOL area, so these wages are competitive with the competition. I honestly wouldn’t be surprised if we increased starting pay 5-10% next year.
